description: Sea-Level Rise and Coastal Land Use in Hawai'i: A Policy Tool Kit for State and Local Governments is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by University of Hawai'i Sea Grant College Program; NOAA Office for Coastal Management | Pacific Region. Hawai‘i is expected to experience sea level rise of one foot by 2050 and three feet by the end of the century; sea level rise of this magnitude poses significant economic, social, and environmental challenges. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Coastal. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
